summary: Istanbul is a tight pick-up-and-deliver game where you move your merchant around a modular market grid, dropping off assistants to trigger repeatable actions while racing to collect rubies. The Big Box bundles both expansions (Mocha & Baksheesh, Letters & Seals), adding tile variety and route options without diluting the crisp, tense core loop.
praised: excellent tension from a limited number of assistants
high replayability from the modular board
expansions add welcome variety without bloating play time
criticised: early turns can feel constrained and samey
some analysis paralysis chasing the optimal route
expansions can slow the pace slightly for newer players

interaction.kind: shared tile spaces and light blocking
interaction.detail: Players move across the same board and can land on tiles already occupied by an opponent (paying them a small bonus) or beat them to the last needed good, but each player otherwise builds up goods and money on their own personal mat.

subsystems: ruby collection via bazaar contracts and deliveries
sources: bonus rubies from special tiles and bonus cards
scoring.how_you_win: Players move their merchant and assistants around the bazaar tiles gathering and delivering goods to complete contracts, each paying out rubies; the first player to collect the target number of rubies (typically 5) immediately wins.
